# pbs_api_token (Resource)

Manages an API token of a Proxmox Backup Server user, such as the token a Proxmox VE cluster backs up with. Its ID is `<user ID>!<token name>`, and it authenticates with that ID and its secret, `value`.

~> **A token has no privileges of its own.** It acts with the intersection of its user's privileges and those of ACL entries for the token ID itself, so it needs `pbs_acl` entries whose `auth_id` is `tokenid`, besides those of its user. Deleting the token deletes its ACL entries.

~> **The secret is stored in state.** PBS shows a token's secret only when it creates the token or regenerates its secret, so the provider keeps it in Terraform state, marked sensitive, for other resources to use — such as the PBS storage of a Proxmox VE cluster. Protect the state accordingly. An imported token has no `value`: change `regenerate` to get a new secret.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pbs_user" "pve" {
  userid  = "pve@pbs"
  comment = "PVE cluster"
}

# The token a Proxmox VE cluster backs up with. Its secret, value, is in
# Terraform state, marked sensitive.
resource "pbs_api_token" "pve" {
  userid     = pbs_user.pve.userid
  token_name = "cluster1"
  comment    = "Backups of cluster1"

  # Any change of this value has PBS generate a new secret; the old one stops
  # working at once. With the hashicorp/time provider, a time_rotating
  # resource's id rotates it on a schedule.
  regenerate = "2026-10"
}

# A token has no privileges of its own: it acts with those of its own ACL
# entries that its user has too.
resource "pbs_acl" "pve_user" {
  path    = "/datastore/store1"
  auth_id = pbs_user.pve.userid
  role    = "DatastoreBackup"
}

resource "pbs_acl" "pve_token" {
  path    = "/datastore/store1"
  auth_id = pbs_api_token.pve.tokenid
  role    = "DatastoreBackup"
}

# PVE's PBS storage signs in with the token ID as the user name and the
# secret as the password.
output "pve_storage_username" {
  value = pbs_api_token.pve.tokenid
}

output "pve_storage_password" {
  value     = pbs_api_token.pve.value
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `token_name` (String) Name of the token, unique for its user: letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, starting with a letter, digit or `_`. Changing it replaces the token.
- `userid` (String) User ID of the user the token belongs to, such as `alice@pbs`. Changing it replaces the token.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the token may sign in. Defaults to `true`.
- `expire` (Number) When the token expires, in seconds since the Unix epoch, such as the `unix` attribute of a `time_offset` resource; `0`, the default, means never. A token also stops working when its user is disabled or expires.
- `regenerate` (String) Any value; changing it to another value — from none included — has PBS generate a new secret, and the old one stops working at once. A `time_rotating` resource's `id` rotates the secret on a schedule. Removing it changes nothing.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `tokenid`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.
- `tokenid` (String) Token ID, `<userid>!<token_name>`, such as `alice@pbs!ci`: what an ACL entry for the token names, and the user name it signs in with. Known at plan time.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The token's secret, as PBS shows it when it creates the token or regenerates the secret. A client signs in with `tokenid` and this secret, as the HTTP header `Authorization: PBSAPIToken=<tokenid>:<value>`; the provider's own `api_token` takes `"<tokenid>:<value>"`. Null after an import, until `regenerate` changes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_api_token.pve
  identity = {
    tokenid = "pve@pbs!cluster1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `tokenid` (String) Token ID, such as `alice@pbs!ci`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_api_token.pve
  id = "pve@pbs!cluster1"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# API tokens are imported by token ID, <user ID>!<token name>. PBS never shows
# a token's secret again, so an imported token has no value until regenerate
# changes, which replaces the secret.
terraform import pbs_api_token.pve 'pve@pbs!cluster1'
```
